text: Article 32(1) of the Constitution of the Republic of Moldova guarantees each citizen freedom of thought and of opinion, as well as freedom of expression in public through words, images or other available means.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE

text: Article 32(2) of the Constitution of the Republic of Moldova provides that freedom of expression shall not be prejudicial to the honour or dignity of others or the right of others to have their own opinion.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE

text: Article 32(3) of the Constitution of the Republic of Moldova provides that the law prohibits and punishes the calling into question and defamation of the State and the nation, calls to war and aggression, national, racial or religious hatred, and incitement to discrimination, territorial separatism, or public violence, as well as any other expression which endangers the constitutional order.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE

text: Article 40 of the Constitution of the Republic of Moldova provides that all meetings, demonstrations, rallies, processions or any other assemblies are free, but they may be organised and take place only peacefully and without the use of weapons.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE

text: Section 6(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be conducted peacefully, without any sort of weapons, and the protection of participants and the environment must be ensured, without impeding the normal use of public highways, road traffic or the operation of businesses, and without degenerating into acts of violence capable of endangering public order or the physical integrity or life of persons or their property.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE

text: Section 7 of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be suspended in circumstances including: denial and defamation of the State and of the people; incitement to war or aggression and incitement to hatred on ethnic, racial or religious grounds; incitement to discrimination, territorial separatism or public violence; and acts that undermine the constitutional order.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE

text: Section 8(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies may be conducted in squares, streets, parks and other public places in cities, towns and villages, and also in public buildings.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE

text: Section 8(2) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct an assembly in the buildings of public authorities, local authorities, prosecutors' offices, courts or companies with armed security.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE

text: Section 8(3)(a) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct assemblies within fifty metres of the Parliament building, the residence of the President of Moldova, the seat of the Government, the Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court of Justice.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE

text: Section 8(3)(b) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that it shall be forbidden to conduct assemblies within twenty-five metres of the buildings of the central administrative authority, the local public authorities, courts, prosecutors' offices, police stations, prisons and social rehabilitation institutions, military installations, railway stations, airports, hospitals, companies which use dangerous equipment and machines, and diplomatic institutions.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE

text: Section 8(4) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that free access to the premises of the institutions listed in section 8(3) shall be guaranteed.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE

text: Section 8(5) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the local public authorities may, if the organisers agree, establish places or buildings for permanent assemblies.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE

text: Section 11(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that not later than fifteen days prior to the date of the assembly, the organiser shall submit a notification to the Municipal Council.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE

text: Section 11(2) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the prior notification shall indicate: the name of the organiser and the aim of the assembly; the date, starting time and finishing time; the location and access and return routes; the manner in which the assembly is to take place; the approximate number of participants; the persons responsible for the proper conduct of the assembly; and the services the organiser asks the Municipal Council to provide.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW AND PRACTICE
